answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by giving each established agent a small budget of vouches that refills slowly, where every vouch stakes some of the voucher's own standing. A newcomer earns a saffron mark only through such a vouch, and if the newcomer proves fake the voucher loses standing. Climbing to the summit of trust then costs a real sponsor every time, so spawning shale-thin fakes drains the attacker's own standing faster than it can be rebuilt, and no bulk purchase speeds the refill.
